sections.html:
Braintree is a South Shore community in Norfolk County with 39,143 residents (2020 census), about 14.6 square miles of land and water. Quincy lies to the north, Weymouth to the east, Holbrook to the south and Randolph to the west. South Shore Plaza is the best known retail destination, and Pond Meadow Park, Sunset Lake and part of the Blue Hills Reservation supply open space.

The town has two historic village centers, Braintree and South Braintree, and ZIP codes 02184 and 02185. The population grew from 10,580 in 1920 to 35,050 in 1970, so much of the housing was built in those decades, and when an older family home passes to heirs who live elsewhere, a quick sale can avoid showings and staging.

Officially it is the Town of Braintree, yet it has been a city under Massachusetts law since 2007, with a mayor and a town council. When you look for paperwork, note that the Assessors, the Collector and the Treasurer all sit under Municipal Finance on braintreema.gov.

sections.h2: Getting to Boston and the Cape
sections.html:
Braintree station is served by the MBTA Red Line, two commuter rail lines (the Fall River/New Bedford Line and the Kingston Line) and the seasonal CapeFLYER. The Weymouth Landing/East Braintree station on the Weymouth border is served by the Greenbush Line.

Interstate 93 and US 1 come in from Boston on the Southeast Expressway and head west toward Route 128. Route 3 splits south toward Cape Cod as the Pilgrims Highway, and Routes 37 and 53 are the other principal highways in town. A house close to the Red Line or an expressway ramp appeals to commuters, so say so when you talk to buyers.

Braintree averages about 48.6 inches of precipitation and about 61 inches of snow in a season, and totals swing widely. Nor'easters are the main storm threat, and thunderstorms from May to September can bring large hail and damaging winds. Roofs, gutters and basements draw the most questions from buyers' inspectors.

The Braintree Assessors publish these rates per $1,000 of assessed value:

Property classRate per $1,000
Residential$10.06
Commercial and industrial$21.39
Personal property$21.33

The Assessors' office is at 1 John F. Kennedy Memorial Drive, phone 781-794-8050. It helps owners with exemption forms, abatement forms and abutter lists, and it runs a property record website. Town Hall is open Monday, Wednesday and Thursday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Tuesday until 7 p.m., and Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m.

An abatement application must be filed on or before the due date of the first actual tax bill, which is generally February 1 where bills are quarterly. Check your schedule on your bill.

File an abatement application with the Braintree Assessors first. They have three months to act. If they deny it or do nothing, you have three months to appeal to the Appellate Tax Board.

  • Pay the tax bill on time, or the board may not hear the case, with limited exceptions.
  • Hearings are held at the board's office in Boston or by video, and most single family hearings last one to two hours.
  • A case usually takes four months to a year to reach a hearing.
  • You must show the home's fair cash value is below its assessed value, and comparable sales help.

If you are selling soon, the appeal may not finish before closing. Ask your attorney how any refund is handled.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Norfolk County
sections.html:
Braintree is in Norfolk County. The Norfolk County Registry of Deeds collects $2.28 in excise tax for each $500 of the sale price or fraction of it when the deed is recorded.

  • The registry lists a $156 fee to record a deed in recorded land and $155 in registered land.
  • The excise tax needs its own attorney's check or bank check, separate from the recording fee.
  • A municipal lien certificate has an $81 recording fee at the registry.
  • Documents filed electronically avoid the $1 postage charge.

A sale needs a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate of compliance from the Braintree fire department. Call once you have a closing date, and expect a fee. Alarms that are past their date or lack a date must be replaced.

Massachusetts treats real estate closings as work for an attorney, and about 80 to 90 percent of properties are recorded land filed at the registry. A home inspection can be part of the deal, and state rules prevent a seller from requiring a buyer to waive it on certain residential sales.

If the house has a septic system, Title 5 calls for an inspection within two years before the sale. Check whether your property has one.

1. Call the Assessors at 781-794-8050 to confirm your assessed value and any exemption or open abatement.
  2. Ask Municipal Finance for your tax balance and request a municipal lien certificate if your attorney needs one.
  3. Check whether the house has septic.
  4. Book the fire department certificate once a date is set, and replace any expired alarms first.
  5. Have your attorney arrange two checks at the registry: one for the excise tax and one for the recording fee.

Cash Home Buyers buys Braintree houses as they are, so a direct sale cuts out showings, staging and repair negotiations. The tax payoff, the alarm certificate and the recording still happen at closing.

faqs.q: Is Braintree a city or a town?
faqs.a: Both. Its official name is the Town of Braintree, but it has had a mayor and council government since 2007 and counts as a city under Massachusetts law.

faqs.q: What is the residential tax rate in Braintree?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2026 the Braintree Assessors list $10.06 per $1,000 of assessed value for residential property.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax in Norfolk County?
faqs.a: The Norfolk County Registry of Deeds charges $2.28 for each $500 of the sale price or fraction of it.
Braintree station has the Red Line, the Fall River/New Bedford and Kingston commuter rail lines, and seasonal CapeFLYER service. The Greenbush Line stops at Weymouth Landing/East Braintree.

faqs.q: Do I need a fire department certificate to sell a house in Braintree?
faqs.a: Yes. The local fire department must certify that smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the sale rules.
